name: fabric-automation-toolchain
about: What the factory loads into every session and every job: agent skills, MCP servers and command-line tools, and the rules that decide which of them each mode may use. Design 3.13 and HR-9. Edit this file by hand and run `python scripts/toolchain.py lock` to resolve it into toolchain.lock.json.

dev.summary: A person at a keyboard, signed in as themselves, working against a sandbox workspace.

agent.summary: The untrusted agent plane (design K4). No credential, no network. Skills come from the pinned pack and MCP servers are local, offline and read-only (HR-3, HR-9).

executor.summary: The trusted plane (K6, K7, K10). Identities come from workload identity, never from a person. MCP servers are read-only here, and every write is a typed executor operation (HR-2, HR-8).

vscode.title: Visual Studio Code with GitHub Copilot

tools.needed_for: everything (fetching the skill repositories with a private configuration needs 2.32)
MCP servers that are npm packages (the Fabric server's README asks for Node.js 22 or later)
the Bicep MCP server (dotnet tool exec)
the Fabric CLI that the git-integration skill calls
the report skill, which names it a required helper for packing, unpacking, validating and previewing reports

skill_sources.title: Microsoft Skills for Fabric
skill_sources.notes: The plugins also bundle MCP servers (unpinned, and with a name that both plugins use for different servers). The kit takes the skills only and defines its own MCP servers below. Skills of both plugins link to a folder named common at the root of the fabric-skills plugin (as ../../common/), so the kit pins that folder in the lock and installs it once beside the skills folder of each host.

skill_sources.title: Microsoft Azure Skills
skill_sources.notes: The azure plugin bundles the Azure MCP server at an unpinned version. The kit takes the skills only.

quarantine.reason: It authors ontology definitions as entity JSON, which the design takes to be the old experience of ontology; Learn says that experience retires on 2027-01-31 (design 3.10, 3.13).

mcp_servers.title: Fabric MCP Server (local)
mcp_servers.summary: Offline Fabric documentation, API specifications and item definitions, plus OneLake, core and Data Factory operations that need a sign-in.

read.summary: Every read-only tool: documentation, core, OneLake and Data Factory.

full.summary: Every tool, including create, update and delete.

mcp_servers.title: Fabric core MCP (hosted)
mcp_servers.summary: Workspace, folder, item, role and capacity management as the signed-in user.

default.summary: All tools of the hosted server. A person signs in through the browser.

mcp_servers.title: Fabric IQ MCP (hosted)
mcp_servers.summary: Read-only questions over Power BI reports and semantic models. The header pins the contract (the URL version does not).

default.summary: Consumption tools. Delegated sign-in only: service principals are not supported.

mcp_servers.title: Power BI Authoring MCP (local)
mcp_servers.summary: Semantic model authoring and validation on local PBIP and TMDL files, or on a model in the service.

offline-readonly.summary: Read-only validation of local model files. No sign-in and no network.

service-readonly.summary: Read-only access to a model in the service as a service principal.

interactive.summary: Read and write, with a browser sign-in and a confirmation before each model edit.

mcp_servers.title: Power BI Authoring MCP (hosted)
mcp_servers.summary: The hosted twin of the local server, for models in the service.

default.summary: Read and write semantic models as the signed-in user.

mcp_servers.title: Fabric SQL endpoint MCP (hosted)
mcp_servers.summary: T-SQL against a warehouse or a lakehouse SQL endpoint. The tool is named executeSQL on the Learn page and execute_query in the tool list of the skills repository's .github/plugin/marketplace.json, so its name is pinned by the contract check, not by this file. The id is not fabric-sqlendpoint on purpose: the Fabric plugin bundles a server of that name, and a host lets the plugin's server replace a project one of the same name.

default.summary: T-SQL statements as the signed-in user. The Learn page does not classify the tool as read-only, so it is treated as able to write.
All tools, with the default Azure credential chain.

mcp_servers.title: Azure MCP Server
mcp_servers.summary: Azure resource tools by service namespace.

full.summary: All tools, including the ones that change resources.

mcp_servers.title: Bicep MCP Server
mcp_servers.summary: Bicep authoring help: resource type schemas, formatting, build and best practices. It launches through `dotnet tool exec`, which needs only the .NET 10 SDK on the path: the `dnx` script that Learn describes sits in the SDK folder, and on the hosted runner image that folder is not on the path. The 10.0.403 SDK takes `--yes` and does not pass it on to the tool (run on Windows with a package from a local feed), although neither its help text nor Learn, which says .NET 11, lists it. The declared environment turns off what the .NET CLI does on its first use by a user (a banner on the error stream, usage telemetry and a development certificate), and an operator's own setting wins. A hosted run launched it against the real package (0.48.1) and its 14 tools are in the lock; the server names itself with a host-like name and a four-part version, which the probe records as `unknown`.

default.summary: All tools. Its offline behaviour is not verified, so its network class is internet.

mcp_servers.title: Azure Resource Manager MCP, cost toolset (hosted)
mcp_servers.summary: The hosted Azure Resource Manager server with the toolset that the Azure cost skills call (their text names it azure-resource-manager-mcp). The server as a whole can also deploy and change resources, and the header only selects the cost toolset (the Azure cost plugin's own configuration), so the variant is declared read-write because nothing here could measure the toolset without a sign-in.

default.summary: Cost and pricing queries. A person signs in; the sign-in method is not documented in the plugin's configuration.

mcp_servers.title: Microsoft Learn MCP (hosted)
mcp_servers.summary: Search and fetch Microsoft Learn pages and code samples. No sign-in.

default.summary: Documentation search, fetch and code samples.

update.policy: A refresh is a pull request, never an automatic change. `update --check` reports what changed upstream and what that breaks; `update --write` rewrites the lock only when the profiles still verify.
